In plain terms: the flow reports positive setup and hold slack in all 9 corners. Hold margin is smallest in the fast (ff) corners, at about 0.11 ns. Whether REQ-011 is met is for the runtime STA check (Chronos) to decide.

## Open issues

1. No congestion/overflow number in the inputs.
2. Signoff DRC and LVS (REQ-013) are not in the inputs.
3. Smallest hold slack 0.11395409938206096 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95: positive, small margin.
4. Post-CTS setup slack at nom_ss_100C_1v60 was 1.5699468835983306 ns; post-route it is 2.056888051435302 ns. The inputs do not explain the difference; Chronos should confirm the signoff value.
5. STA corners and sky130A release are open questions in the spec; the 1.0 ns skew target is not in the spec.
assumptions: The single entry in reports/pnr_iterations.json (iteration 1, tag it1) is the final P&R state; no other iterations exist.
setup_ws_by_corner and hold_ws_by_corner in pnr_iterations.json are post-route worst slacks in ns as reported by the flow's STA; positive means the path meets the constraint.
route_drc_errors is the detailed-router DRC count, not a Magic/KLayout signoff DRC on the final GDS.
antenna_violating_nets/pins are from the flow's antenna check after routing.
utilization 0.507475 in pnr_iterations.json is post-placement/route cell utilization (including inserted buffers), which is why it is higher than the floorplan utilization 0.484219.
The 1.0 ns CTS skew target (cts_target_ns / target_ns) comes from the tool data, not from the spec.
open_issues: No routing congestion or global-route overflow number is present in any input file, so the congestion state cannot be reported from data; the runtime or a report containing overflow should supply it.

route_drc_errors 0 is the router's count. REQ-013 requires 0 DRC violations and 0 LVS mismatches on the final GDS; signoff DRC and LVS results are not in the inputs and must come from the real runtime checks.
Smallest hold slack is 0.11395409938206096 ns at min_ff_n40C_1v95 (all three ff corners are between 0.11395409938206096 and 0.11866688523257896 ns): positive but small margin.

Post-CTS setup slack at nom_ss_100C_1v60 was 1.5699468835983306 ns (cts_report.json) but the post-route value in pnr_iterations.json is 2.056888051435302 ns; the inputs do not explain the increase (possibly the 22 timing-repair buffers or different parasitics). Chronos (STA) should confirm which is the signoff number.
The spec leaves the sky130A release and STA corner list open; this report uses the 9 corners present in the tool data.
The 1.0 ns CTS skew target is not stated in the spec; a human should confirm it.
